CVE-2026-105152.title: Apache Roller: Weblog template access to wrapped objects exposes another user's password hash
CVE-2026-105152.description: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows a weblog administrator to read another user's stored password hash by authoring a custom weblog template that reaches the wrapped persistent object behind the template's weblog or entry data, rather than the reduced set of fields the wrapper is meant to expose. Roller treats weblog administrators as untrusted and exposes weblog and entry data to templates only through wrapper classes, but a public accessor on those wrapper classes returned the underlying persistent object directly, including the stored password hash of the weblog's creator and of any author whose entry renders on the page. CVE-2026-118446.title: Use-after-free in INSTRUX array members in pybddisasm
CVE-2026-118446.description: A use-after-free vulnerability in the pybddisasm Python bindings affects array-valued members of INSTRUX objects, including ND_OPERAND arrays. These arrays are exposed as Python lists whose elements reference memory owned by the parent INSTRUX object. Retaining a list or an element does not keep the parent allocation alive. Accessing an element after the parent INSTRUX object has been freed therefore accesses freed memory. Depending on how the element is used and whether the freed allocation has been reused, this may expose process memory or cause the Python process to crash. Exploitation requires an application to retain and subsequently access an array element after the parent object has been freed. The pybddisasm package is no longer maintained.

CVE-2026-119210.title: MariaDB Connector/J: LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE file check could be satisfied by text inside quoted identifiers, letting a malicious server read client files
CVE-2026-119210.description: MariaDB Connector/J is used to connect applications developed in Java to MariaDB and MySQL databases. From 3.0.0 until 3.3.7, 3.4.5, and 3.5.11, the ClientMessage.validateLocalFileName() check used a regular expression that could match LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE text inside quoted identifiers, string literals, or comments instead of requiring a real statement. A malicious or compromised server, or a machine-in-the-middle attacker, could return crafted database or table identifiers that the connector reused in metadata or updatable-result queries, then answer with a LOCAL INFILE request for a client file. With allowLocalInfile enabled, this caused the connector to stream any readable client-host file named by the crafted text, including through DatabaseMetaData.getImportedKeys(), DatabaseMetaData.getExportedKeys(), or ResultSet.updateRow() paths. This issue is fixed in versions 3.3.7, 3.4.5, and 3.5.11.

CVE-2026-99332.title: HID: core: Fix out-of-bounds left shift by 32 in s32ton()
CVE-2026-99332.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: core: Fix out-of-bounds left shift by 32 in s32ton()

Syzbot reported an out-of-bounds shift (32-bit integer shifted left by
32) in the s32ton() routine in the HID core. This routine converts a
signed 32-bit integer to a signed n-bit integer, and it caps the value
of n at 32. But when n == 32 there's no need to do anything; it can
simply return the input value. This will avoid calculating (1 << n)
when n is 32, which was the cause of the invalid shift.

CVE-2026-99387.title: smb: client: bound POSIX lock data area by response length
CVE-2026-99387.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: bound POSIX lock data area by response length

CIFSSMBPosixLock() receives a TRANS2 response whose server-provided
DataOffset and DataCount are not required by validate_t2() to describe an
interval inside the response. A server can therefore make the client read a
cifs_posix_lock beyond the response buffer and return those kernel bytes
through F_GETLK.

Use smbCalcSize() to obtain the full response length after any multipart
TRANS2 reassembly, then reject data areas that extend past it before
dereferencing them.
